title: Correctness of the full decision tree
statement: Let $f \colon (\bbf_2)^n \to \{\mathtt{true},\mathtt{false}\}$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables, let $k \le n$, and let $acc, x \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\mathtt{true},\mathtt{false}\}$ be two assignments that agree on every coordinate below $k$, that is $acc_i = x_i$ for all $i < k$. Then the full decision tree for $f$ that branches on variables $k, k+1, \dots, n-1$ starting from the accumulator $acc$ evaluates on input $x$ to $f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: acc and x agree on all coordinates below k
replaced:
For a function $f$, an index $k \le n$, and assignments $acc, x$ agreeing on all
coordinates below $k$ (i.e. $acc\,i = x\,i$ whenever $i.\mathrm{val} < k$), the complete
decision tree $\mathrm{buildFullDTree}\,f\,k\,acc$ evaluates to $f\,x$ on $x$.
